added_failure_mode.description: The catalog names lockfile drift as a no-network, no-second-publisher mode. The required executable tests only reconcile registry ids against installed PACKAGE.json files. If there is no lockfile, an id-xor of zero (or a missing lockfile detector) reads as 'no drift'. That zero is vacuous: lockfile-vs-installed-bytes was not measured. PR-ONLY does not create a lockfile. Absence of the file is not evidence of agreement.
added_failure_mode.required_followup: Add a lockfile detector that fails closed when the lockfile is missing, then compare lockfile hashes to installed PACKAGE.json bytes. Do not treat lockfile drift as addressed by registry-vs-deployed id-xor.
added_failure_mode.title: Absent lockfile reported as zero lockfile drift

strongest_surviving_counterargument: PR-ONLY is a publication policy, not an install reconciler. A single-owner estate that never ships a public index can still carry a committed registry that disagrees with files on disk, a lockfile that is missing, or a leftover tree after a revert PR. Those local modes stay reachable. The surviving preference is that PR review is enough operationally; that preference does not make today's disagreement count zero, and it does not convert public marketplace modes that PR-ONLY makes unreachable into mitigated controls.
